evals.name: refunds-daily-mart
evals.prompt: Finance wants refunds per merchant per day in the warehouse, next to the orders numbers. Can you add it to the nightly pipeline?
evals.expected_output: A refunds model chain (source declaration, staging, mart) wired into the nightly pipeline. raw.refunds, described in docs/sources.md but not declared as a dbt source, is declared with freshness. Staging keeps the latest row per refund id (the loader appends a row per change since 3 August 2026), counts only refunds whose current status is succeeded, dates them by the UTC date of succeeded_at, and converts the rupee numeric amount to integer paise. The figures have one row per day and merchant, never include a day at or after end_date (first build included), and a merchant or a day whose refunds were all reversed loses its row on a later run (a whole-window delete, or a refund-grain table merged on refund id with the rollup rebuilt from it). Because a succeeded refund can be reversed up to 45 days later, each nightly refunds run picks up reversals for at least 45 days, not the orders DAG's 30, yet never reaches back far enough to erase refunds raw has deleted. Any table that is the only copy of old refunds cannot be dropped by --full-refresh. The refund models run after refunds land at 03:00 UTC and are kept out of the 01:00 orders run, which selects +tag:daily (inherited by everything under marts/). A plain dbt run with the default vars (start_date 2024-01-01) must not be able to delete refunds history once raw has dropped it. The final message says history reaches back only about 60 days (raw's retention) and that the oldest few days are incomplete because retention cuts by created_at while the mart dates by succeeded_at. It flags that stg_orders lacks the same deduplication and that the Makefile backfill runs --full-refresh against ADR-0002. dbt and Airflow are not installed here, so only make check (offline pytest) can run; the SQL is judged by reading it. Nothing is committed.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and tests/test_dbt_layout.py and tests/test_dags.py are not weakened (no rule removed, skipped or loosened)

raw.refunds is declared as a dbt source with a freshness check (the fixture's dbt/models/staging/_sources.yml declares only orders and merchants), and every new model reaches it through source('raw', 'refunds'); no model hard-codes a raw.refunds relation name

The refunds staging (or an intermediate model) keeps only the latest row per refund id by _loaded_at (docs/sources.md: the loader appends a row per status change since 3 August 2026), and only refunds whose current status is 'succeeded' are counted: a refund that succeeded and was later reversed contributes nothing

Each refund is dated by the UTC date of succeeded_at (the README's metric definition), not created_at, and the amount is converted from rupees (numeric(12,2)) to integer paise with rounding rather than truncation, so no mart column sums rupees next to paise

The refunds figures finance reads have one row per day and merchant, no mart model calls source() (a refund-grain fact that a daily rollup reads is fine), no new model uses select *, and the tests run with the pipeline cover: not_null on day and merchant, uniqueness of the (day, merchant) grain runnable without new packages (or with a stated package addition), relationships from merchant_id to dim_merchants, non-negative range tests on the measures, and accepted_values for pending, succeeded, failed and reversed on the refund status in the model that carries the status column (staging or a refund-grain model, since a daily mart of succeeded refunds has none); a test may live in a yml or as a singular test

No refunds table finance reads holds a row for a day on or after the run's end_date, on any build including the first, non-incremental one: an upper bound applied only inside is_incremental(), or a daily rollup with no date bound over a refund-grain table, lets a build write the run day's partial refunds. The lower bound may be relaxed on the first build to load raw's history

A refund reversed after an earlier run counted it disappears from the figures on a later nightly run, both a (day, merchant) row whose only refund was reversed and a whole day whose refunds were all reversed: a day-window design deletes the whole [start_date, end_date) window (an explicit window delete, microbatch, or equivalent), not only the keys present in the new batch as delete+insert on (day, merchant) or on day alone does; a design that keeps refunds at refund grain (merged on refund id) and rebuilds the daily rollup from it in full meets this too

A reversal is picked up for every refund that succeeded up to 45 days before the run, because docs/sources.md says a succeeded refund can be reversed up to 45 days after it succeeded: a day-window design rebuilds at least the last 45 days of succeeded dates (reusing the orders DAG's 30 day LOOKBACK_DAYS, the orders edit window, leaves a refund reversed 31 to 45 days after success counted for good), and a refund-grain design merges every refund whose status can still change

The refund models run after raw.refunds lands (03:00 UTC per docs/sources.md): a later schedule, a separate DAG, a sensor or a freshness gate, with the window taken from the run's data interval, never from the current date; and the 01:00 UTC daily_orders run does not build or test the refund models (a model under marts/ inherits tag daily from dbt_project.yml and daily_orders selects +tag:daily, which also pulls in its staging parents)

If the refunds mart deletes a window before inserting, a run with the default vars (start_date 2024-01-01 in dbt_project.yml, which `make dbt-build` and a plain `dbt run` use) cannot erase refund history raw no longer holds once the mart is older than 60 days: the run requires explicit vars, adds a guard, sets full_refresh: false with a bounded default, or states this hazard and the rule operators must follow; a guard that makes the model's rows depend on the wall clock (now() or current_date in its SQL) does not count. If the run removes the default vars or makes `make dbt-build` require a window, the final message says which entry points change

Every table that becomes the only copy of refunds raw has dropped (the daily refunds mart, or a refund-grain table the rollup reads) cannot be rebuilt from raw by `dbt build --full-refresh` or `dbt run --full-refresh`: it sets full_refresh: false (or an equivalent guard), or the final message states the hazard and cites ADR-0002; a table the run rebuilds in full from such a store each night needs no guard

No nightly run erases refunds raw has already deleted: a day-window design keeps its window short enough that every refund with a succeeded date inside it is still in raw (45 days of succeeded dates sits inside the 60 day created_at retention with room for the one to three day lag), or it states the residual case of a refund that took longer to succeed; a window reaching back to raw's retention edge, or a nightly full rebuild of the mart from raw alone, wipes the oldest refunds every night

The final message says the refunds history the first build can produce reaches back only about 60 days, because the loader deletes refunds requested more than 60 days ago (docs/sources.md), so days before that can never be loaded from raw

The run tells the user, in its final message or in a document the final message points to, that the oldest few days of that history are incomplete, because retention cuts by created_at while refunds are dated by succeeded_at, one to three days later; saying only that history starts about 60 days back does not count

If the run adds refund columns to fct_orders_daily instead of a separate model, it deals with that model's on_schema_change='fail' and ADR-0002's ban on --full-refresh (a new model and a swap, or a stated migration step); a separate refunds mart, or a view joining the two marts, needs neither

The final message flags that stg_orders does not deduplicate the loader's appended rows the way the new refunds staging must, so fct_orders_daily likely double counts edited orders since the loader switch; if the run changes how existing fct_orders_daily partitions are computed, it says so and says those partitions then need a backfill

The run flags that the Makefile's backfill target runs dbt run --full-refresh (ignoring start and end), which ADR-0002 forbids because it drops every partition older than raw's 60 days; if the run edits that target, the result rebuilds only the given range, never uses --full-refresh, and fails on an empty or missing range

The final message says dbt parse and dbt build were not run against the warehouse (dbt is not installed), and, if the run changed anything under dags/, that the DAG import was not run (Airflow is not installed); if it ran SQL in a database it started itself, it says what it ran and on what data; it does not claim the models were built or tested against the warehouse or report real refund figures
profiles.yml.example, pyproject.toml, dim_merchants and stg_merchants are unchanged, and no file in the repository gains a literal password or connection string

The run makes no git commit (the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree), and it writes files only inside the repository and its own run folder, not in a shared temp directory or the home directory

If the run records a decision anywhere in the repository (an ADR or a decision note), it is not marked Accepted or approved and names no decider (a person, role or team) who did not make the decision in this conversation, and it does not edit the two existing ADRs' decisions
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: dedupe-edited-orders-backfill
evals.prompt: fct_orders_daily is double counting orders that merchants edited. Started when we switched to the new loader on 3 Aug. Fix it and give me the backfill to run.
evals.expected_output: stg_orders keeps only the latest landed row per order id, with a deterministic tie-break and a unique test that would have caught the bug, and the cancelled filter applies to the current status. fct_orders_daily gets an upper bound on its window and a delete that covers the whole window, so a backfill writes exactly its window and removes rows whose orders are now all cancelled. Affected partitions start at about 2026-07-03, not 2026-08-03, because the first nightly run after the switch (3 August, data interval 2 August) rebuilt 30 days back. But raw keeps only 60 days (docs/sources.md) and deletes by placed_at every night, so for a run on 26 September 2026 only days from about 29 July are still held in full: the backfill starts there, and the days from about 3 July to about 28 July cannot be corrected from raw; rebuilding them with a whole-window delete would erase or understate them. The run says so, lists them and names a route to correct them. The remaining days fall out of raw one a day, so the backfill is urgent. It runs by partition, oldest first, one at a time, with the nightly DAG paused, and never through the Makefile's --full-refresh target, which ADR-0002 forbids. A plain dbt run with the default vars must not be able to delete history raw no longer holds. The backfill is handed to the user, not run. dbt and Airflow are not installed here; nothing is committed.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and tests/test_dbt_layout.py and tests/test_dags.py are not weakened (no rule removed, skipped or loosened)

stg_orders (or a model between it and the marts that every order consumer reads) keeps exactly one row per order_id, the one with the latest _loaded_at, and the cancelled filter and the amount that reach fct_orders_daily come from that latest row, so an order placed and later cancelled is not counted and the README's metric definitions are otherwise unchanged
A data test that would have caught the bug is added: unique on order_id in the deduplicated model (stg_orders's yml has only not_null on order_id at the fixture), at error severity

The deduplication picks the same row on every run when two rows of an order share a _loaded_at (a deterministic tie-breaker, or a test that fails on such ties); a row_number over _loaded_at alone that is only noted in the report does not count, since a unique test cannot catch a pick that flips between runs

The run says the affected partitions start at about 2026-07-03, not 2026-08-03, with the reason: the first nightly run after the switch (3 August, data interval 2 August) rebuilt a window reaching 30 days back (LOOKBACK_DAYS in dags/daily_orders.py, the 30 day edit window in docs/sources.md), so orders placed from early July gained appended rows and were rebuilt with them; 2026-07-04 with a stated reason is fine

The run computes the oldest day raw.orders still holds in full from the 60 day retention in docs/sources.md and its own date (for a run on 26 September 2026, orders placed before about 28 July are deleted, so the first complete day is about 29 July; a day either side with a stated reason is fine), and the backfill it hands over starts at that day, not at 2026-07-04

The final message says the affected days older than that (from about 3 July to the day before the oldest complete day) cannot be corrected from raw, gives that range, keeps them out of the backfill (rebuilding a day raw no longer holds in full erases or understates it, and with a whole-window delete a missing day is wiped), and names what could correct them (for example a re-export from the source system) or that finance must be told those days stay overstated; it never claims the backfill corrects every affected day

The final message says the backfill is urgent: raw loses one more day every night at 00:10 UTC, so each day not rebuilt before it leaves raw stays wrong, and the oldest recoverable day is lost within about a day of the run

No command handed to the user uses --full-refresh, and the Makefile's backfill target (which runs dbt run --full-refresh and ignores start and end) is either changed to rebuild only the given range, failing on an empty or missing range, or explicitly called out as unsafe, citing ADR-0002

fct_orders_daily's window gains an upper bound (order_date < end_date) and its delete covers the whole [start_date, end_date) window (an explicit window delete, microbatch, or equivalent), so a backfill removes both a (day, merchant) row whose orders are now all cancelled and a day whose orders are all cancelled; delete+insert on ['order_date', 'merchant_id'] or on order_date alone replaces only keys present in the new batch. A run that keys on order_date alone passes only if it states the empty-day gap and gives a step that clears it

The run's evidence that the backfill clears stale rows covers a day whose orders are now all cancelled (a test it adds, SQL it ran against a database it started, or a worked row-by-row trace in its report), not only a merchant whose orders were cancelled while others on that day remain

If the run makes fct_orders_daily delete a whole window, a run with the default vars (start_date 2024-01-01 in dbt_project.yml, which `make dbt-build` and a plain `dbt run` use) cannot erase partitions raw no longer holds: the run requires explicit vars, adds a guard, sets full_refresh: false with a bounded default, or states the hazard; a guard that makes the model's rows depend on the wall clock (now() or current_date in its SQL) does not count. If the run removes the default vars or makes `make dbt-build` require a window, the final message says which entry points change

The backfill runs oldest first and one day or window at a time (`airflow backfill create` with --max-active-runs 1, a DAG change to max_active_runs=1, or a sequential loop), and the run tells the user to pause daily_orders during the backfill and unpause it after, or otherwise prevents the nightly run and the backfill writing the same days at once
The run does not execute the backfill or any dbt command against a warehouse; it gives the user the exact command or commands to run, with the dates filled in

The final message says dbt parse and dbt build were not run against the warehouse (dbt is not installed), and, if the run changed anything under dags/, that the DAG import was not run (Airflow is not installed); if it ran SQL in a database it started itself, it says what it ran and on what data; it does not claim the mart is corrected, report corrected figures or state a number of affected orders or an amount it never computed
The run adds no refunds models or other features the request did not ask for, and leaves profiles.yml.example, pyproject.toml, dim_merchants and stg_merchants unchanged

The run makes no git commit (the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree), and it writes files only inside the repository and its own run folder, not in a shared temp directory or the home directory

If the run records a decision anywhere in the repository (an ADR or a decision note), it is not marked Accepted or approved and names no decider (a person, role or team) who did not make the decision in this conversation, and it does not edit the two existing ADRs' decisions
